review_candidates.title: National Data Adviser with Ministry of Social Affairs Beirut NORCAP
review_candidates.description: Job Description NORCAP works to improve aid to better protect and empower people affected by crisis and climate change. We do this by providing expertise and solutions to humanitarian, development and peacebuilding partners, because we believe working together is the best way to reduce needs, risks and vulnerability over time. We seek and promote more effective ways of working at the global level and in the field. NORCAP’s aim is not only to reduce needs, but also to create choice and opportunity for vulnerable people. NORCAP works with and through our partners to improve aid in two complementary ways: We provide targeted expertise to strengthen our partners’ response. We collaborate with partners to develop solutions to un-met gaps and challenges. This role supports NORCAP’s commitment to strengthening evidence-based decision-making and improving the quality of services delivered to people affected by crisis through trusted data and actionable analysis. The Ministry of Social Affairs (MoSA) in Lebanon manages large-scale data systems that support both emergency response activities and national social protection programmes, including AMAN and the Social Safety Nets programme. The ministry is currently addressing challenges related to fragmented datasets, data quality, validation processes, and the need for reliable analytical outputs to support operational and strategic decisions. The Role The National Data Adviser will provide focused technical support to strengthen the quality, reliability, and usability of priority datasets within the Ministry of Social Affairs. Working closely with ministry teams, the successful candidate will clean and validate critical datasets, develop practical analytical tools, and produce decision-ready outputs that improve programme planning and implementation. Success in this role will be measured through the delivery of high-quality datasets, dashboards, analytical products, and documentation that support continuity beyond the assignment. The position is based in Beirut, Lebanon, on a 12-month contract with the possibility of extension subject to funding and performance. The role reports to the Ministry Line Manager and the NORCAP Thematic Manager. As the National Data Adviser, you will take on the following responsibilities: Role And Responsibilities Engage with Ministry of Social Affairs leadership, technical teams, and stakeholders to identify priorities, define methodologies, and develop a realistic workplan. Assess priority datasets, systems, tools, and existing analytical products to identify data quality issues, inconsistencies, duplication, and operational risks. Clean, validate, reconcile, and maintain priority datasets, with particular attention to displacement, beneficiary, and payment-related data. Design and implement practical data cleaning, validation, and deduplication approaches, including the development of scripts and methodologies where appropriate. Develop, improve, and maintain decision-ready dashboards and analytical products that support operational and strategic decision-making. Produce analytical briefs and insights on key trends, geographic coverage, and programme performance, presenting findings to stakeholders for review and validation. Develop clear documentation, standard operating procedures, guidance materials, and handover packages to support continuity and sustainable use of data products. Ensure compliance with data protection and confidentiality standards while contributing to knowledge sharing, collaboration, and other NORCAP priorities. Qualifications And Experience To excel in this role, candidates should possess the following qualifications and skills: 5 to 7 years of professional experience in data analysis, data management, or a closely related field, including work with large and complex datasets. Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality analytical outputs and results within challenging timelines and evolving operational contexts. Strong technical proficiency in Python and/or R, SQL, Power BI and/or Tableau, and advanced Microsoft Excel. Proven experience in data cleaning, validation, deduplication, data visualisation, and the development of decision-support products. Experience within humanitarian, emergency response, social protection, public sector, or government data systems is highly desirable. Strong analytical, communication, prioritisation, and problem-solving skills. Please read the attached terms of reference for more details before applying. What We Offer In recognition of your expertise and contributions, we provide the following benefits and opportunities: Rewarding work for a renowned global organisation Access to a network of humanitarian, peace, and development professionals A dedicated Staff Care Unit Eligible for consideration for NORCAP membership and future assignments, subject to a successful performance review. How To Apply Based on what you have read so far, do you think you could be a good fit? If so, please follow these steps and apply! When submitting your application, kindly register in English your full employment history and education. Please include your full name as written in your passport. Uploaded CVs alone will not be reviewed. NORCAP reserves the right to conduct a full background check on shortlisted candidates. Approved Health Certificate will be required prior to contract commencement and assignment. Feedback will be given to all applicants within four weeks after the closing of this advertisement. Apply before 22.09.2026, 23:59 (Oslo time). We look forward to receiving your application! Our Values & Commitment NORCAP is part of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC). All NRC employees are expected to act in accordance with the organisation’s values. Being dedicated, innovative, inclusive, and accountable are behaviours and beliefs that guide how we work and how we build relationships. We are committed to creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, empowered, supported, and a genuine sense of belonging. NORCAP values diversity, equity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. We believe that a diverse workforce strengthens our ability to respond effectively to the needs of people affected by crisis. NRC has a zero-tolerance stance toward any form of exploitation or abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH) , and we do not tolerate inaction when concerns arise. All offers are subject to reference and background checks conducted in line with our safeguarding standards, and NORCAP reserves the right to conduct a full background check on shortlisted candidates. About The Team At NORCAP, we work to better protect and empower people affected by crises and climate change. With expertise in the humanitarian, development and peacebuilding sectors, we collaborate with local, national and international partners on finding solutions to meet the needs of people at risk.
